title: X++ statements: switch fallthrough and comma case lists, break scope inside a loop, while/do-while/for
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a class DemoStatusRouter that pins the X++ statement rules that differ from C#. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="switch-loops"). Confirm the SalesStatus enum values with get_object_info before writing them - do not guess. All methods public static. (1) `int route(SalesStatus _status)` - a switch over SalesStatus that returns a routing code. It must use a COMMA-SEPARATED case list for the two statuses that share a code, must end every branch with `break`, and must contain exactly ONE deliberate fallthrough whose comment says it is deliberate and what it falls into. X++ switch FALLS THROUGH without break - the opposite of C# - so an accidental missing break FAILS this case; a `default:` branch is required here. (2) `SalesId firstMatching(SalesStatus _status)` - a `while select` over SalesTable with the switch from rule (1) inside it. When the switch decides the record is the wanted one it must set a flag, and the loop must be left by testing that flag AFTER the switch: a `break` written inside the switch leaves only the SWITCH, not the loop, and FAILS this case. (3) `int countDown(int _from)` - a `do { } while (...);` loop, which runs its body once even when _from is already zero, and a comment saying that is the difference from `while`. (4) `int sumTo(int _limit)` - a `for` loop using `continue` to skip odd numbers. Nothing in this class may use `pause` or `window` (removed keywords, they are compile errors) or carry a `client`/`server` modifier (parsed but ignored - delete them in new code). Every user-visible string must come from strFmt with a label. The class must build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
